stem.text:
Which of the following device(s) produce(s) light by bombarding gaseous substances inside with electrons?
	(1)	Compact fluorescent lamp
	(2)	Light emitting diode
	(3)	Incandescent lamp

answer.worked:
In a CFL, there are a small amount of mercury and an inert gas under a very low pressure. During the process of the generation of light in a CFL, electrons ionize the inert gas atoms by bombarding them to form ions and more free electrons. The electrons in the mercury atoms are excited when the atoms are bombarded with electrons and ions.
∴ (1) is correct.

	(1)	The electrons in mercury atoms inside the lamp are excited.
	(2)	Electrons are emitted from the negative electrode.
	(3)	Ultra-violet radiation is emitted by the excited electrons in mercury atoms.

answer.worked:
In a CFL, there are a small amount of mercury and an inert gas under a very low pressure. When a high voltage is applied across the two electrodes, electrons are emitted from the negative electrode. The electrons ionize the inert gas atoms to form ions and more free electrons. The electrons in the mercury atoms are excited when the atoms are bombarded with electrons and ions. When the excited electrons jump to lower energy levels, energy is released mainly in the form of ultra-violet radiation.
∴ (1), (2) and (3) are correct.
